title: Multi-modal single-cell RNA sequencing on M. tuberculosis-infected mouse lungs
author: Pisu, Russell
materials: Chromium Next Gem Single Cell 3′ GEM Kit

steps.title: Obtain lung single‑cell suspension
steps.instruction: Follow steps 4–18 of the previously published protocol to obtain a lung single‑cell suspension.

steps.title: Wash cells and transfer to tubes
steps.instruction: Slowly remove the supernatant, resuspend the cells in 2 mL washing solution, transfer the suspension to 2 mL Eppendorf screw‑cap tubes, and centrifuge at 500 × g for 3 min at 20–25 °C.

steps.title: Optional Fc‑blocking incubation
steps.instruction: If using surface‑marker staining, resuspend the pellet in 1 mL Fc‑blocking solution (washing solution + anti‑CD16/32), incubate 15 min at 4 °C, then centrifuge at 500 × g for 3 min at 20–25 °C.

steps.title: Antibody staining of cells
steps.instruction: Remove supernatant, resuspend the pellet in washing solution containing the antibody mix at the recommended concentration, incubate 30 min in the dark at 4 °C, add 600 µL washing solution and mix 5–6 times, centrifuge at 500 × g for 3 min at 20–25 °C, wash with 1 mL washing solution and centrifuge again at 500 × g for 3 min, resuspend in sorting buffer to achieve >80 % sorting efficiency, and pass the suspension through a 30 µm cell strainer. Keep all samples at 4 °C or on ice.

steps.title: Prepare low‑bind tubes with buffer
steps.instruction: Fill each 1.5 mL low‑bind Eppendorf tube (one per sorted sample) with 600 µL Cell Staining Buffer (Biolegend). Typical sorting volume is ~300 µL for ~60,000 cells.

steps.title: Sort cells into buffer tubes
steps.instruction: Set up sorting gates as shown in Figures S1A–S1C, keep the output tubes at 4 °C during sorting, and sort the cells directly into the prepared tubes.

steps.title: Spin and block sorted cells
steps.instruction: Immediately after sorting, centrifuge the tubes at 500 × g for 5 min at 20–25 °C. While spinning, prepare a blocking solution (e.g., for 4 samples mix 2 µL TruStain FcX™ PLUS with 198 µL Cell Staining Buffer). Carefully remove the supernatant first with a wide‑bore 1 mL pipette tip, then finish removal with a 200 µL tip without disturbing the pellet. Resuspend each pellet in 50 µL blocking solution and incubate 15 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare HTO‑ADT antibody mixes
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL each HTO Totalseq antibody to the corresponding sample tubes. For the ADT pool, add 2 µL of each ADT antibody to Cell Staining Buffer up to a final volume of 196 µL (if >100 ADT antibodies, no volume adjustment). Spin the ADT pool at 8,000 × g for 15 s, mix 5–6 times, aliquot 49 µL of the pool into each HTO tube, mix, then spin each HTO‑ADT mix at 8,000 × g for 15 s.

steps.title: Add HTO‑ADT antibodies to cells
steps.instruction: After the 15‑min block, add 50 µL of the corresponding HTO‑ADT antibody mix to each sample, pipette up/down 5–6 times, and incubate 30 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash cells post‑staining
steps.instruction: Add 300 µL chilled Cell Staining Buffer to each tube, centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 min at 20–25 °C, carefully remove the supernatant without touching the pellet, and repeat the wash once more.

steps.title: Resuspend and methanol‑fix cells
steps.instruction: Resuspend each pellet in 150 µL chilled DPBS, then add 1,350 µL frozen 90 % methanol (final volume 1.5 mL) drop‑by‑drop while rocking the tube to fix the cells.

steps.title: Store fixed cells
steps.instruction: Store the methanol‑fixed cells at –20 °C for up to one week or at –80 °C for long‑term storage.
